title: Why Raising a Kid Actually Costs $300,000
alts: The Hidden $300,000 Price Tag of Having a Baby
Why Daycare Costs More Than Your Rent
line1: Having a baby? Researchers say raising one kid to age eighteen costs about $300,000. Here's where every dollar actually goes.
summary: Dave and his partner are expecting a baby, and the crib alone is $499. We break down where the real $300,000 price tag (Brookings/LendingTree, birth to age 18) actually comes from: the baby gear markup on strollers, car seats and cribs; the recurring diaper-and-formula bill; why Child Care Aware of America finds daycare beats rent or a mortgage in most states; and the biggest, most invisible cost of all -- lost wages and the 'motherhood penalty' on a parent's career. Then: practical ways to lower the bill, from secondhand gear to daycare co-ops, employer benefits and a 529 plan. Education, not advice.
